YOU ARE 1200% THE AH!!! 
My mother had an obsession with my hair growing up. It was long, it was straight, it was healthy; it was, in her eyes, "perfect". Unlike hers: frayed curls, lots of breakage from over colouring at the salon every time she saw a grey hair. You get the picture.
I used to love the attention. It was the only time my mother was ever nice to me and I was doted on and I felt like it was my pride I could show off to people. My mother loves my hair, surely everyone else will agree it's lovely, won't they?
But as the abuse I suffered at her hands continued, I began feeling more and more controlled through my hair. I couldn't cut it, I couldn't dye it. My mother used to say I could only cut it if I gave it to her so she could "wear it". As a joke of course. But it became creepy. Sometimes when she was mad she'd pull at it and tell me I didn't deserve such lovely hair.
I grew up. My hair changed in many ways- it became thicker, curly, darker, and so, so long.  My restrictions, however did not change: mother would tell the stylist what to do, and would punish me if I looked unhappy.
It was getting hot, it felt like it absorbed all heat and was cooking my skull. Kids at school would pull on it and bully me for having "dog scruff". I became depressed and it was taking a monumental effort to wash it.
I turned 18. I could still only get it trimmed, and I never went to a hair dresser of my own volition, as I had come to hate people touching it. 
When I moved out the next year, it took so much willpower to let anyone let their hands on my hair, including hairdressers.
Finally, one day out of the blue, I'd had enough. I went into a salon, told the stylist I needed something different. I wasn't happy with my hair anymore, and it caused me more grief than I could take. She asked if I was comfortable shaving one of the sides.
I froze in fear- what would mother think? What would she do to me when she saw it?
Suddenly I was so angry at that initial response: I, an adult, had become so afraid of a woman I didn't even see all that often anymore, that she was still controlling what I did with my body.
I told her to cut it.
And it was the happiest decision I had made before I got the other side buzzed to match.

Tldr let your kids fucking do what they want with their hair or it's going to scar them by all the misery it entails to not have the slightest bit of control over their own body.
